theater: 蘇美爾南部拉格什與烏瑪

battle.name: 第二次烏瑪獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 蘇美爾南部拉格什與烏瑪
battle.brief: 約公元前2400年，蘇美爾的烏瑪城邦在第一次抗爭失敗後再度挑釁：其君伊爾改動拉格什的界渠、拔除界碑，恩特梅納遂聯合烏魯克出兵將其打敗，並以重新劃界與盟誓收場，是已知最早的城邦邊界戰爭之一。卡面是早王朝時期的埃及長矛，即與此役同時的近東通行銅矛形制。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前二十四世紀末蘇美爾南部城邦之間的第二次邊界衝突，交戰方是南部沖積平原上的拉格什城邦與其北面的鄰邦烏瑪，時間落在早王朝第三期。拉格什方面由城邦總督恩特梅納率領，銜銜是蘇美爾的恩西，即執掌城邦者而非王；他在本役的關鍵動作是聯合烏魯克的國王盧加爾-基尼舍-杜杜出兵，烏魯克王繼承恩沙庫沙那，並見於《蘇美爾王表》。烏瑪方面先後由伊爾（楔形文字作 UŠ，部分文本亦作烏什）與埃納卡列執政：伊爾是發動挑釁的一方，戰敗後由埃納卡列出面議定疆界。兩城位置互為犄角：一般認為拉格什在今 Tell al-Hiba、烏瑪在今 Tell Jokha，爭議地帶「梅沙」落在兩者之間，約二十餘公里；北面是尼普爾與基什，東面是埃蘭，西方遠及幼發拉底上游的馬里與埃布拉商路。蘇美爾此時沒有常備軍，雙方戰力來自城民徵召兵、依附神廟的常備戰士，以及以野驢、馬拉曳引的四輪戰車隊；盟約與界約由神廟祭司與書記官起草，並以諸神之名背書。
countriesEn: This war was the second border conflict between the city-states of southern Mesopotamia in the late twenty-fourth century BC, fought between Lagash on the southern alluvial plain and its northern neighbour Umma, in the Early Dynastic III period. The Lagash side was led by the city governor Entemena, whose title was the Sumerian ensi, that of a governor of the city rather than of a king; his decisive move in this campaign was to take the field in alliance with Lugal-kinishe-dudu, ruler of Uruk, who had succeeded Enshakushanna and appears in the Sumerian King List. Umma was ruled in turn by Il, written with the sign UŠ and also rendered Ush in some texts, and by Enakalle: Il was the one who raised the challenge, and after his defeat Enakalle came forward to negotiate the new border. The two cities lay at opposite angles of the same canal system: Lagash is generally identified with Tell al-Hiba and Umma with Tell Jokha, and the disputed strip called Mesha lay between them, some twenty-odd kilometres across; to the north stood Nippur and Kish, to the east Elam, and to the west, far up the Euphrates, the trade routes of Mari and Ebla. Sumer had no standing army at this time, and the strength of both sides came from citizen levies, full-time warriors attached to the temples, and four-wheeled war wagons drawn by donkeys or onagers; treaties and boundary agreements were drafted by temple priests and scribes and were countersigned in the names of the gods.
people: 核心人物是拉格什的恩特梅納，楔形文字作 En-teme-na，意為神聖的秩序。他是恩納圖姆家族的後人：羅浮宮銀器銘文稱他為恩納圖姆之子，而拉格什戰爭錐體的銘文又稱恩納圖姆是他的伯父，學者因此認為兩處所指未必是同一位恩納圖姆。他在早王朝第三期至少統治十九年，接過家族對烏瑪的軍事優勢。他的戰爭銘文現藏羅浮宮，編號 AO 3004，錐面約四十餘行，是最早把城邦邊界衝突完整記錄下來的文獻之一；內容宣稱行動出自恩利爾的堅定命令，寧吉爾蘇是恩利爾的戰將，戰果被寫成恩利爾投下大網。對面的伊爾在文中被斥為竊田妄言，並被指自行宣稱界渠屬己、要把界壩從安塔蘇拉移到埃迪姆伽拉布祖，銘文則強調恩利爾與寧胡爾薩格並未把這份權力賜給他。議和方是烏瑪的埃納卡列；更早的仲裁者是基什王梅西利姆，他在伊什塔蘭的命令下丈量田地、豎立界碑，而恩特梅納以與埃納卡列劃定疆界作結。學術方面，2015年薩拉伯杰與施拉坎普合編的論文集重譯並重估了這批戰爭銘文，認為它所記正是烏瑪第二次爭取獨立的戰爭；1916年尼耶斯在《美國東方學會學報》發表耶魯網紋圓柱的專論，確立該器與錐體銘文同文。
peopleEn: The central figure is Entemena of Lagash, written En-teme-na, meaning the divine order. He belonged to the family of Eannatum: the inscription on the silver vase in the Louvre calls him the son of Eannatum, while the war cone of Lagash names Eannatum as his uncle, and scholars have therefore doubted whether the two references point to the same man. He ruled for at least nineteen years in the Early Dynastic III period and inherited the family's military advantage over Umma. His war inscription is kept in the Louvre under the number AO 3004; its cone surface carries a little over forty lines, and it is one of the earliest documents to record a conflict between city-state borders in full. Its content claims that the action was carried out by the firm command of Enlil, that Ningirsu was Enlil's warrior, and that the outcome was Enlil throwing his great net. On the other side Il is branded as one who steals fields and speaks evil, and is accused of claiming the boundary channels as his own and of announcing that he would shift the boundary levee from Antasura to Edimgalabzu, while the text insists that Enlil and Ninhursag had not given him that power. The party to the settlement was Enakalle of Umma; the earlier arbiter had been Mesilim of Kish, who at the command of Ishtaran measured the field and set up a stele, and Entemena closed the affair by fixing the border with Enakalle. On the scholarly side, a 2015 volume edited by Walther Sallaberger and Ingo Schrakamp re-translated and re-evaluated these war inscriptions and argued that they record precisely Umma's second war of independence, while in 1916 James B. Nies published a study of the Yale net cylinder in the Journal of the American Oriental Society, establishing that its text is identical to that of the cone.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬早王朝時期的長柄刺器，銅或青銅矛頭以繩纏或榫接綁在木杆上；前王朝末至早王朝初的埃及與蘇美爾同屬一個冶金世代，兩地矛首都可見套接式空腔柄的形制。蘇美爾一方的裝備與之極為接近：矛頭分長短兩種，另有銅斧、匕首、銅鏃與燧石箭頭的弓、投石索、骨柄銅錘，以及木框蒙皮或柳條編織的盾牌；烏爾軍旗戰爭一側所繪的步兵正是持矛方陣，同側還有四輪戰車，由野驢或馬拉曳引，車上設箭手，這是早王朝已知最接近戰車的形態，而真正的輕型戰車要到公元前二千年中期才出現。本役是邊界與灌溉之爭，未見攻城器械的記載，若有圍堵也只需截斷對方的渠道與渡口，而非強攻城牆；真正關鍵的器材是界碑、界渠、界壩與分水口，銘文點名的安塔蘇拉與埃迪姆伽拉布祖兩處界壩，正是爭端要爭的物件。補給靠河道與渠道行船，軍糧取自拉格什與烏瑪各自的田地，銅料靠北方的馬里與埃布拉商路交換；真正稀缺的是鐵，全場兵器只有銅、燧石、骨與木。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is an early dynastic long thrusting weapon, a copper or bronze blade bound to a wooden shaft by cord or tang, and the late Predynastic to early dynastic Egypt of that moment and Sumer belonged to a single metallurgical horizon, socketed hollow-tang spearheads appearing on both sides. The Sumerian armoury was extremely close to it: spearheads of two lengths, copper axes, daggers, bows with copper or flint arrowheads, slings, maces with bone handles, and shields of wood frames covered with hide or woven from reeds; the war side of the Standard of Ur shows precisely a phalanx of spearmen and, on the same side, four-wheeled war wagons drawn by donkeys or onagers with archers aboard, the closest thing to a chariot known in the early dynastic period, true light chariots not arriving until the middle of the second millennium BC. This campaign was a quarrel over boundary and irrigation, and no siege engines are recorded: any blockade would have had to cut the enemy's canals and fords rather than assault city walls. The truly decisive pieces of equipment were the boundary stele, the boundary channels, the levees and the water division offtakes, and the two levees named in the text, Antasura and Edimgalabzu, were precisely the objects in dispute. Supply moved by boat along the river and the canals, the army drew grain from the fields of Lagash and Umma alike, and copper came through exchange with Mari and Ebla in the north. What was genuinely scarce was iron: every weapon on the field was of copper, flint, bone and wood.
tactics: 本役的戰術可以從銘文用語還原出骨架。第一步是水權與界線的破壞：伊爾一方先動界渠，把水從寧吉爾蘇界渠與南碩界渠改道，繼而拔除梅西利姆所立界碑，逕向拉格什平原推進，這在蘇美爾的邦國邏輯中等於向對方宣戰，等同撕毀共同承認的裁定。第二步是外交施壓：恩特梅納先派使臣赴烏瑪交涉，結果被指竊田妄言，使節無功而返，說明糾紛已從灌溉分配升級為主權爭端。第三步才是出兵：拉格什聯同烏魯克，藉恩利爾的堅定命令把軍事行動呈現為執行神諭、恢復既定疆界，而非以力奪利，因此銘文反覆出現神名與正當命令的措辭。作戰層面，銘文以恩利爾的戰將投下大網描述全殲，學者多解作包抄與封鎖：車隊與步兵在平原上合圍潰散之敵，截斷其退回渠道的路線，再以壘土收埋陣亡者。戰後程序同樣關鍵：重新豎立界碑、丈量田界、由祭司在神前見證，並把處罰條款寫死在圓柱上，違約者將被寧吉爾蘇的大網罩住，這段文字因此被視為已知最早的盟約文本。
tacticsEn: The skeleton of the tactics can be recovered from the wording of the inscription. The first step was the violation of water rights and of the border: Il's side moved the boundary channels first, diverting water out of Ningirsu's channel and Nanshe's channel, and then pulled down the stele that Mesilim had set up, marching straight for the plain of Lagash, which in the logic of the Sumerian cities amounted to a declaration of war, the destruction of a judgement both sides had accepted. The second step was diplomatic pressure: Entemena first sent envoys to Umma to argue the matter, and they were dismissed as thieves of fields and speakers of evil, which shows that the dispute had been lifted from irrigation into sovereignty. Only then came the resort to arms: Lagash marched in alliance with Uruk, presenting the military action as the execution of a god's command and the restoration of an established border rather than as a seizure by force, which is why the gods' names and the formula of the just command recur throughout the text. At the level of combat, the inscription describes a total victory as Enlil's warrior throwing his great net, which scholars generally read as encirclement and blocking: the wagon corps and the infantry closed around the routed enemy on the plain, cut off the road back to the channels, and then raised mounds over the fallen. The postwar procedure mattered just as much: the stele was re-erected, the fields were re-measured, the terms were witnessed before the god by the priests, and the penalty clause was fixed in writing on the cylinder, the violator to be caught in Ningirsu's great net, a passage therefore treated by some scholars as the earliest surviving treaty text.
data: 本役可核對的數字極少，且多為器物與文本的物理數據而非戰況數據。年代方面，戰爭表把烏瑪第二次爭取獨立定在公元前2400年，屬早王朝第三期，該期一般以公元前2500至2350年為界；恩特梅納的在位年數至少十九年。文本方面，羅浮宮錐體銘文編號 AO 3004，通行定名 RIME 1.09.05.01，抄本約四十餘行；耶魯巴比倫收藏的網紋圓柱與錐體同文，另有多件泥板與器物殘片可對勘；恩特梅納的玄武岩坐像高七十六厘米，側面與背面的刻銘證明其早王朝的身分；其銀質三足器現藏羅浮宮編號 AO 2674，器腹飾鷹徽，頸部作獅噬北山羊與鹿的浮雕。地理方面，一般以 Tell al-Hiba 為拉格什、Tell Jokha 為烏瑪、Tell Uruk 為烏魯克，Tell Jokha 在瓦爾卡西北約六公里，與 Tell al-Hiba 相距約二十餘公里，爭議的梅沙正落在兩城之間的渠道帶。本役的兵力、損失數字、交戰地點與具體日期在文獻中均無記載；前一次戰爭中三千六百這類數字出自宣傳體銘文，不能套用於本役。
dataEn: Very few figures can be checked for this campaign, and most of them are physical facts about the objects and texts rather than about the fighting. As to date, the list of wars places Umma's second war of independence at 2400 BC, in the Early Dynastic III period, which is generally bounded by 2500 to 2350 BC; Entemena's reign lasted at least nineteen years. As to texts, the Louvre cone inscription is number AO 3004, conventionally cited as RIME 1.09.05.01, and its copy runs to a little over forty lines; the net cylinder in the Yale Babylonian Collection carries identical text, and several further tablets and object fragments can be collated against it. Entemena's diorite seated statue is seventy-six centimetres high, and the inscriptions on its side and back confirm his early dynastic identity; his silver tripod, now in the Louvre as number AO 2674, carries the eagle crest of Lagash on the body and a relief around the neck of lions devouring ibexes and deer. As to geography, Lagash is generally taken as Tell al-Hiba, Umma as Tell Jokha and Uruk as Tell Uruk or Warka, with Tell Jokha lying some six kilometres north-west of Warka and about twenty-odd kilometres from Tell al-Hiba, so that the disputed Mesha fell in the belt of canals between the two cities. Troop numbers, losses, the precise site of the engagement and its exact date are simply not recorded in the sources; the figure of three thousand six hundred that belongs to the earlier war is a boast of a propagandistic inscription and cannot be carried over to this one.
cause: 起因要分前後兩層。前一層是上一次爭取的殘餘：恩納圖姆的戰役把烏瑪壓服，界碑由基什王梅西利姆豎立，烏瑪被迫接受拉格什主導的邊界安排，烏瑪在王表上不再出現，說明它一度失去獨立的政治地位；第二次爭取獨立正是要推翻這一安排，但方式不是正面攻城，而是從水利下手。直接導火線是伊爾改動界渠：把水從寧吉爾蘇界渠與南碩界渠改道，等於奪走拉格什一方的灌溉份額，並在田間爭議中以界渠屬我自居，聲言要把界壩從安塔蘇拉移到埃迪姆伽拉布祖；恩特梅納派使交涉反被指為竊田妄言，邊界與水利同時被撕破，戰爭遂不可免。深一層是拉格什自身的需要：恩特梅納要把父輩靠刀兵取得的優勢，轉成由諸神見證、可以長久維持的盟約，因此必須先打贏，再重新劃界。
causeEn: The causes have to be taken in two layers. The first is the residue of the previous attempt: Eannatum's campaign had subdued Umma, the stele was set up by Mesilim of Kish, and Umma was forced to accept a boundary arrangement under Lagash's leading; it no longer appears on the king list, which shows that it had for a time lost the standing of an independent polity. The second attempt at independence was meant to overturn that arrangement, but not by frontal assault: it began with water. The immediate spark was Il's tampering with the boundary channels, diverting water out of Ningirsu's channel and Nanshe's channel, which meant taking away Lagash's share of irrigation, while in the argument over the fields he claimed for himself that the boundary channel was his and announced that he would shift the boundary levee from Antasura to Edimgalabzu; Entemena's envoys were met with the charge of stealing fields and speaking evil, so that both the border and the water were openly broken and war became unavoidable. Deeper still was Lagash's own need: Entemena wanted to convert the advantage his family had won by force into a compact guaranteed by the gods and capable of lasting, which is why the war had to be won first and the border drawn afresh afterwards.
impact: 本役的長遠影響大於戰術意義。它把邊界從口頭的權力宣示變成可以丈量、可以立碑、可以用盟約文本固定的物件，並在蘇美爾外交中確立一種可複製的格式：神名背書、界碑為憑、違約以神罰相威脅，耶魯的網紋圓柱因此被一些學者視為已知最早的盟約文本；這套格式在往後數百年裡反覆出現在拉格什與烏瑪之間的年度記錄中，最後濃縮成《鴿子之碑》上那段著名的界線協議。制度上，本役也標示了蘇美爾城邦政治的成熟形態：拉格什與烏瑪的首領都只是城邦總督，真正的王權在基什、尼普爾與烏爾等處，於是城邦之間不再爭王位，而是爭灌溉與地界，並且靠神廟的書記官、丈量員與外交使團來處理。考古上，Tell al-Hiba 的發掘與 Tell Jokha 的探掘，把早王朝第三期的南部網絡重新拼出來，使早王朝的年代學不再只依賴單一王表。
impactEn: The long-run consequences of this campaign outrun its tactical meaning. It turned the border from a verbal claim of power into something that could be measured, marked with a stele and fixed in a treaty text, and it established in Sumerian diplomacy a repeatable format: the gods' names as guarantee, the stele as evidence, a divine penalty to threaten any violator, which is why the Yale net cylinder is treated by some scholars as the earliest surviving treaty text; the same format recurs in the annual records kept between Lagash and Umma over the following centuries and finally condenses into the famous boundary agreement on the Stele of the Vultures. Institutionally the campaign also marks the mature shape of Sumerian city-state politics: the heads of Lagash and Umma were merely city governors, while real kingship sat in Kish, Nippur and Ur, so the cities no longer fought over thrones but over irrigation and land, and settled such things through temple scribes, surveyors and embassies. Archaeologically, excavation at Tell al-Hiba and exploration at Tell Jokha have reassembled the southern network of the Early Dynastic III period, so that the chronology of the era no longer rests on the king list alone.
result: 銘文給出的結局很明確：寧吉爾蘇在恩利爾的戰令下投下大網，在拉格什平原上為烏瑪的敗軍壘起墳塋；伊爾被擊敗，烏瑪的第二次爭取獨立失敗；最後由恩特梅納與烏瑪的埃納卡列重新劃定疆界，界碑復立，網紋圓柱則把這一安排連同神罰條款寫定存證。也就是說，拉格什贏得的是邊界與水權的確定，烏瑪保住了城與政權，卻沒有換回獨立；這也解釋了後來為何烏瑪在拉格什衰落後迅速坐大，最終在盧加爾扎克西手上反過來滅掉拉格什。至於戰役本身的細節，兵力、損失、交戰地點與持續時間史料完全空白，只能從銘文的語氣與器物的形制去推測，任何具體數字都沒有根據。
resultEn: The outcome stated in the inscription is plain: at Enlil's command in war his warrior threw the great net and raised mounds for the defeated of Umma upon the plain of Lagash; Il was beaten, Umma's second attempt at independence failed, and in the end Entemena fixed the border with Enakalle of Umma, the stele was re-erected, and the net cylinder wrote the arrangement and its divine penalty down as evidence. Lagash, in other words, won the settlement of the border and the water rights, while Umma kept its city and its government but got no independence back; that in turn explains why Umma grew so rapidly once Lagash declined, and in the end destroyed Lagash in its turn under Lugal-zage-si. As for the details of the fighting itself, the strength of the armies, the losses, the place of the engagement and how long it lasted, the sources are simply silent, and only the tone of the inscription and the shape of the objects allow any inference; no specific figure can be founded on evidence.
